summary.headline: Permanent Magnets Q4 standalone revenue rose 47% YoY to INR 66 crores; FY26 revenue INR 225 crores (+13%), with Relays ramp pushed to H2 FY27.
summary.overview: Standalone Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was INR 66 crores, up 47% YoY, while FY26 revenue was INR 225 crores, up 13%. FY26 EBITDA margin was 17% versus 14% a year earlier, helped by product mix and second-half scale-up; Q4 margin was 15%, up YoY but down sequentially. The new Alloys furnace was installed in January and commercialised in Q4, while the Relays project slipped to commercial ramp from H2 FY27 and no rare-earth revenue was booked in FY26 due to Chinese export restrictions. Management guided FY27 revenue growth of 20-30% with EBITDA margin of roughly 15-18%.

financial_highlights.change: no sales due to China export restrictions
CFO disputed INR 85 crores figure; includes USD 5 million ECB in subsidiary

segments.name: Alloys
segments.commentary: New furnace installed January FY26, commercialised in Q4; utilisation about 80-90% from installation to year-end. Management expects FY27 volume roughly 3-4x FY26 levels. Q4 sales were mostly virgin-metal alloy, which carries slightly lower margin than scrap-based product.

segments.name: Relays (electricity meter relays)
segments.commentary: Commercial ramp delayed to H2 FY27 from earlier timelines; testing and customer approvals still in progress. Management estimates INR 25-50 crores of FY27 revenue at near-full utilisation of the initial 5 million unit capacity, with a possible step-up to 10 million units. Per-meter value cited at INR 250-300; TAM for 25 crore meter replacement put at INR 6,500-7,000 crores.

segments.name: Quantum Magnetics (rare-earth magnets)
segments.commentary: Phase 1 (assembly) implemented. Phase 2 (block cutting, machining, surface treatment) due Q3-Q4 FY27, with commercial sales mainly from Q4 FY27. Long-term plan of 5,000 tonnes, with value of INR 3,000-4,000 crores cited, expected around FY30-31. Assembly revenue of INR 10-15 crores estimated for Q4 FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue growth guided at 20-30%, with possibility of higher depending on Alloys and Relays orders.
FY27 EBITDA margin guided at roughly 15-18%, similar to the current level.
Relays commercial business expected to pick up pace only in the later part of FY27; sales expected after September 2026 per management judgment.
Rare-earth assembly revenue estimated at INR 10-15 crores in Q4 FY27.

Planned FY27 capex of INR 40-50 crores for PML standalone and another INR 40-50 crores for Quantum (about USD 5 million contribution over roughly 18 months), with funding mix of debt and equity yet to be finalised.
capex_capacity: Capex to date: about INR 18 crores on Alloys and INR 5-6 crores on Relays (testing and end-of-line equipment done; production equipment partly pending and tied to orders).
New consolidated factory in Vasai (Ahmedabad highway) to combine six Mumbai-area plants; about INR 20 crores of the Quantum-related spend earmarked for it, land already acquired.
Relays capacity being set up in phases: first 5 million units, then 10 million depending on orders.
Quantum Magnetics Phase 2 capex (block cutting, machining, surface treatment) expected in Q3-Q4 FY27; powder-to-block project in planning stage.
Management plans about INR 30 crores of FY27 capacity additions for Alloys and Relays, tied to customer requirements.
demand_pricing: H2 FY26 top-line recovery led by Alloys, with exports recovering after first-half weakness from US tariffs; energy meter demand was weak in H1.
EV demand from European and American customers softened; Chinese EV makers dominate growth and PML has no sales to China yet.
Customers are shifting from heavy to light rare-earth options, which management sees as helpful for future orders.
Competition in Alloys comes from a few listed and unlisted players; PML targets smaller capacities and import substitution.
Around 5-6 companies are expected to enter the magnet business, with some applying for the PLI scheme; PML has not yet applied and is still evaluating schemes.

qa_highlights.question: Will the government's rare-earth PLI scheme bring capex incentives?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is still evaluating the scheme and multiple options; the decision on whether and which scheme to apply for is expected in the next few weeks.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue and margin from rare earths in FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: No revenue in FY26 because Chinese export restrictions blocked magnet imports; revenue expected to start in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Alloys utilisation and FY27 ramp?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation was about 80-90% after the January installation; FY27 volumes expected at 3-4x FY26. Product mix between virgin metal and scrap to be clearer by end Q1 or Q2 FY27, with virgin metal (lower margin) dominant in Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Relays peak revenue and utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 revenue of INR 25-50 crores possible from the initial capacity at near-100% utilisation, depending on customer orders; average value per meter INR 250-300.

qa_highlights.question: Debt level jump from INR 15 crores to INR 85 crores?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO disputed the INR 85 crores figure, saying standalone debt is about INR 20 crores; the increase relates to a USD 5 million ECB in a subsidiary for capex.

qa_highlights.question: Long-term Quantum Magnetics scale and timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Long-term plan of 5,000 tonnes, valued at INR 3,000-4,000 crores at sale prices; commercial sales mainly from Q4 CY27, with scale-up around FY30-31 subject to Phase 2 execution and demand.

risks_watch: Relays timeline has already slipped; testing and customer approvals are still pending, and first meaningful sales depend on H2 FY27 orders.
Rare-earth business depends on Phase 2 execution and on the China export regime; no sales yet and no PLI decision.
Alloys mix is skewed toward lower-margin virgin metal; product mix will be clearer only by end Q1 or Q2 FY27.
Capex funding mix (debt vs equity) for about INR 80-100 crores across standalone and Quantum is not finalised; consolidated debt figures were disputed on the call.
Management could not give revenue beyond FY27 and said it cannot comment on FY28 numbers; prior commercialisation timelines have repeatedly slipped.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the Alloys ramp and the long-term rare-earth plan, but cautious and vague on timelines and numbers: Relays, PLI participation and FY28 outlook were repeatedly qualified as dependent on orders. Management also acknowledged prior delays, and the CFO's correction of the debt figure was firm.
key_quotes: We would put the estimate between 20% to 30% and then plus something maybe.
We are setting up the Relays plant phase-wise. Our first investment is going to be for 5 million capacity, and then we will increase it to 10 million capacity depending on which orders we get.
There was no revenue in FY26 because of the restrictions from China for export of magnets.

adds.what: New Alloys furnace (installed Jan FY26, commercialised Q4 FY26); FY27 volume expected 3-4x FY26 levels
Relays initial 5 million unit capacity (phase 1), possible step-up to 10 million units depending on orders
Quantum Magnetics Phase 2 (block cutting, machining, surface treatment)
New consolidated Vasai factory combining six Mumbai-area plants (about INR 20 crore earmarked from Quantum-related spend; land acquired)

growth.why: FY27 consolidated revenue growth guided at 20-30% (midpoint 25%) with EBITDA margin 15-18%, backed partly by the Alloys furnace running at ~80-90% and volumes expected at 3-4x, plus Relays INR 25-50 crore FY27 revenue from H2 FY27, but Relays timing has slipped and Quantum sales start only in Q4 FY27 with no rare-earth revenue in FY26.
